messages.subject: Moderated path analysis???
parts:
Dear all, 

I want to test the moderator path analysis. 
Could I directly use the product of moderator and X? Or do I need center the mean of X and moderator and then to get the product?

My path model is following:
model_id_moderator <- '
     #regression
     Z ~ Y1 + Y2 + Y3
     Y1 ~ X1 + X1*Moderator
     Y2 ~ X1 + X2
     Y3 ~ X2 + X3
     #correlation
     Y1 ~~ Y2 + Y3
     Y2 ~~ Y3
'
Thanks. 

Best Regards,
Sun

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderated path analysis???
parts:
I want to test the moderator path analysis. 
Could I directly use the product of moderator and X? Or do I need center the mean of X and moderator and then to get the product?

My path model is following:
model_id_moderator <- '
     #regression
     Z ~ Y1 + Y2 + Y3
     Y1 ~ X1 + X1*Moderator
     Y2 ~ X1 + X2
     Y3 ~ X2 + X3
     #correlation
     Y1 ~~ Y2 + Y3
     Y2 ~~ Y3
'

Centering X1 and Moderator at their means only sometimes has the convenient result of lowering the correlation between the product term and each of the mean-centered variables.  Regardless, you will have to calculate the product term manually so it is included in your data.frame, then use the name of that product-term variable in your syntax.  For example,

dat$X1_Moderator <- dat$X1 * dat$Moderator

So you could simply calculate the product term from raw variables and again from mean-centered variables, then look at the correlation matrix among the product variables and the raw and mean-centered X1 and Moderator to see whether it even makes a noticeable difference. 

Also, in your syntax, make sure to include all lower-order terms if they are involved in interactions.  Your current syntax constrains the effect of Moderator to be zero when X1 == 0 (i.e., change the line "Y1 ~ X1 + X1*Moderator" to "Y1 ~ X1 + Moderator + X1_Moderator").

Terry
